document.title: Taliban Under Pressure
document.authors: Karl F. Inderfurth, Assistant Secretary of State for South Asian Affairs, to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Memo says the Taliban's hold on power may be slipping, citing reports of growing political opposition in Herat and Paktia, internal dissent and unpaid civil servants. Albright wrote in the margin: "This is encouraging. Let's discuss when you come back." Pakistan's support remains firm; Russia and Turkey are working against extremism.

key_claims: The Taliban face growing domestic opposition, including tribal uprisings in Paktia and Herat, and their hold on power may be slipping.
Cracks within the Taliban ranks include sabotage of aircraft in Kabul and guards reportedly aiding Ismail Khan's escape, though Mullah Omar remains in control.
UNSCR 1267 sanctions on Ariana Airlines angered Afghan traders formerly supportive of the Taliban.
Pakistan's support for the Taliban remains firm even as Russia and Iran step up opposition.
Russia and Iran pressed Masood to allow Dostam to return to organize Uzbek resistance.
The US is promoting Zahir Shah's Rome initiative and a loya jirga as an alternative, with $500,000 in ESF funds.
